title_sub: Guess which one breaks the scale

rungs.label: Being left-handed
rungs.context: About 1 in every 9 people you meet

rungs.label: Rolling double sixes
rungs.context: Two dice, 36 combos, and only one is 6-6

rungs.label: A hole-in-one
rungs.context: For an average golfer on a par 3

rungs.label: Being dealt a royal flush
rungs.context: Deal a hand every minute: about 15 months to see one

rungs.label: Winning the Powerball jackpot
rungs.context: One ticket every drawing: about 1.9 million years
rungs.source: Powerball official odds; 3 drawings a week

rungs.label: A random Rubik's Cube is solved
rungs.context: One scramble a second: 1.4 trillion years, 100x the age of the universe

rungs.label: A shuffled deck in one exact order
rungs.context: More possible orders than atoms on Earth (about 10^50)

outro_top: The rarest one is in your kitchen drawer.
outro_line: Every good shuffle is almost certainly an order no one has ever seen before.

hook.top: Shuffle a deck and the order you get had odds of
hook.bottom: It has probably never existed before in history.
hook.loop: Let's climb from everyday to impossible...
